insider_note: The heart rate rises as well as the breathing rate. Most answers give only the breathing.

Breathing and Exchange of Gases · 2 marks

steps.label: Less oxygen at height
steps.why: The share of oxygen in air does not change with height; it is the total air pressure that falls, so each breath holds fewer molecules.
common_mistakes: Writing that the air has less oxygen by percentage. The pressure is what falls.
Saying breathing becomes easier at height.
steps.memory_tip: Higher up, thinner air, less oxygen in every breath.
steps.margin_note: Two lines on the cause before the response.

So a man going up a hill gets less oxygen

steps.label: The body's response
steps.why: Two rates rise together: breathing brings more air in and the faster heart carries it round more often.
common_mistakes: Giving only the breathing rate. The heart rate rises too.
steps.memory_tip: Breathe faster and beat faster to make up the oxygen.
steps.margin_note: Both rates are marked. Name them separately.
